summary: Adds signed tenant application eligibility projections and fail-closed runtime admission across interactive and asynchronous plugin work.
userImpact: Tenant application activation remains independent per tenant, while paid plugin execution additionally requires a current eligible state.
Self-hosted plugins declaring no entitlement provider continue to use the existing activation behavior.
Expiry and revocation stop new work without deleting retained plugin data.

instructions: Run the normal database migrations before enabling signed tenant eligibility.
Keep eligibility enforcement disabled unless a workload issuer and verification keys are configured.

configuration: Adds opt-in signed tenant eligibility verification settings; existing self-hosted deployments remain unchanged by default.
Cloud-required deployments must configure the exact issuer, audience, and ES256 JWKS used by the eligibility authority.

changes: Adds a workload-only endpoint for applying a signed tenant/plugin eligibility projection.
Adds safe eligibility state to tenant application responses without exposing price, agreement, or raw signature material.
Requires tenant.apps.use in addition to the manifest-declared action for interactive tenant plugin operations.

notes: The migration adds tenant/plugin eligibility projections without changing tenant activation or plugin-owned data.
Rollback removes only host eligibility projections after SaaS-required enforcement has been disabled.

security: Eligibility JWS values are verified as ES256 against configured issuer, audience, tenant, plugin, release, revision, and time bounds before persistence.
Interactive gateway calls, frontend bootstrap, schedules, events, and contribution refresh all recheck effective availability.
Revocation and stale or invalid eligibility fail closed without deleting tenant plugin data.
documentation: Documents the signed eligibility contract, effective availability equation, workload ingestion, runtime enforcement, configuration, compatibility, and rollback.
knownLimitations: Real GKE and published-artifact qualification is delivered by the Kubernetes and combined cloud slices.
rollback: Disable SaaS-required eligibility enforcement before rolling back the migration.
Do not delete plugin-owned tenant data when removing or expiring an eligibility projection.
validation: Tests cover valid, stale, expired, wrong-tenant, wrong-plugin, wrong-release, wrong-issuer, wrong-audience, and unknown-key projections.
Tests cover different tenant eligibility states for one release and immediate denial of interactive, scheduled, event, and contribution work after deactivation or revocation.
